lessons.intro: Two Rieslings from the same grape can taste like different drinks: one lean and sharp, one ripe and round. The grape is the same. The place is not. When a guest asks why one bottle costs twice the other, the honest answer is often the site: how far from the equator, how high, which way the slope faces, what water is near and what the roots sit in. This picture is the whole story on one slope.

points.p: WSET puts most good vineyards between 30 and 50 degrees of latitude, north or south. Nearer the equator, growers look for something to cool the vines, such as sea breezes or mountain air, or the grapes ripen too fast and lose freshness. Further from the equator, the job flips: they hunt for every bit of warmth and sun. So a cool-climate wine is not a lesser wine. It is a wine made where ripening is the hard part, which is why acidity and lightness are its strengths.

points.h: Altitude and slope: heat in, cold out
points.p: Air cools by about 0.6°C for every 100 m you climb, so Mendoza's vineyards above 1,000 m stay fresh despite the Argentine sun. A slope facing the equator catches more sun. Just as important, cold air is heavy and flows downhill, pooling on the valley floor. North Carolina State University's grower guide calls these low spots frost pockets: on calm, clear nights the temperature can differ by 3 to 5°F (about 2 to 3°C) over 50 feet of height. That is why the best sites sit mid-slope, not at the bottom.

points.h: Water: a mirror and a blanket
points.p: Large bodies of water even out temperature. They warm cold air in winter and cool warm air in spring, which slows bud break and cuts frost risk. A cold ocean cools a warm region, and its morning fog shields vines from strong sun. In the Mosel, Jancis Robinson notes that vines close to the river gain from it acting as a mirror, bouncing extra light onto steep slopes that can top 30 degrees.

Vines want water, but not wet feet. NC State asks for at least 30 to 40 inches of permeable soil so roots can go deep and find water in a dry spell. Stony soils warm up too. Mosel slate is porous: it drains surplus rain and holds the day's heat, then releases it at night. Clay, as in parts of Rioja, holds more water. The trade-off: rich, wet soils give big vines and dilute fruit; lean, free-draining ones give smaller crops with more concentration.

lessons.atWork: Pick two wines by the glass. For each, find the region's latitude, height and soil in two minutes online, then write one line: what the site does to the taste. Give your team the line, not the map. 'High, cool slope, so it stays fresh' sells better than a soil lecture.
lessons.takeaway: A wine's style starts with its place: latitude sets the heat, altitude and slope fine-tune it, water steadies it and soil decides how hard the vine works.

lessons.intro: When a licence goes wrong, it rarely goes wrong at the council desk. It goes wrong when a neighbour, the police or environmental health object and nobody saw it coming. The Licensing Act 2003 sets out exactly who can speak and who decides. If you know the map before you apply, you can talk to the right people first and often avoid a hearing at all.

points.p: The licensing authority is your local council. Under the Act it sets up a licensing committee of 10 to 15 councillors, which can split into sub-committees of three. Officers can handle routine, uncontested work. But the explanatory notes are clear: anything where representations or objections have been made goes to the committee or a sub-committee, not an officer. And if nobody objects, section 18 and the section 182 guidance (para 1.16) say the authority must grant the licence, with conditions that match your operating schedule.

Section 13 lists the bodies that are consulted on every application: the licensing authority itself, the police, the fire and rescue authority, the health and safety enforcing authority, the planning authority, environmental health (pollution and noise), a body that protects children from harm, public health in England, and the Home Office for alcohol and late-night food. Since 29 June 2026, the Greater London Authority is also one for premises in London. Police and environmental health make most of the difference in practice.

Anyone else, such as a resident or a nearby business, is an 'other person'. Under section 18 a representation only counts if it is about the likely effect on the four licensing objectives and arrives within the set period. The council can reject an other person's objection as frivolous or vexatious, but must give reasons. Only the police can object to your designated premises supervisor, and only in exceptional circumstances.

If relevant representations are made, there is a hearing, unless the council, you and every objector agree it is not needed. The sub-committee can grant as asked, change or add conditions, remove one or more licensable activities, refuse your premises supervisor, or reject the application. In London, councils must now send the GLA set information before and after hearings on applications of strategic importance.

lessons.atWork: For one of your sites, write the name of the council, its licensing officer, and a contact at the police licensing team and environmental health. Add the nearest residents' group. That list is your early-warning system for any variation or event notice.
lessons.takeaway: No objection means a licence must be granted. Win the responsible authorities and the neighbours before you apply, and the hearing often never happens.

lessons.intro: Every new restaurant feels it must be everywhere: Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, the lot. Then the posting slips, the accounts go quiet, and a quiet account looks like a quiet room. The better move is to pick one platform where your guests already are, do it well, and add a second only when you can keep it up.

points.p: 125 Data & Insights surveyed 29,190 UK guests in spring 2026. As summarised by Joli, 75% of venue choices came from previous experience (42%) or a personal recommendation (33%). Social media was the named driver for just 4%. The Kitch and KAM State of Social report (January 2026) found 18% of UK adults use social media to research a venue, and 13% visited somewhere unplanned after seeing friends there. So social works best as word of mouth you can see, not as an advert.

Among guests who do use social to choose, the same survey found Instagram most influential at 44%, then TikTok at 25% and Facebook at 13%. Age changes the picture: 54% of 18 to 24-year-olds are TikTok-led when finding venues. Kitch and KAM's follower data agrees. Hospitality brands' biggest Instagram group is 35 to 44 (35%), TikTok's is 25 to 34 (37%) with 28% under 24, and Facebook skews 35 to 54.

points.h: Effort and reach are not equal
points.p: Kitch and KAM's benchmarks from 68 brands show the median brand posting 4 times a week on Instagram, 4 on Facebook and 2 on TikTok. Median daily engagement is 0.2% on Instagram, 2.3% on TikTok and 0.4% on Facebook, but 92% of Facebook views now come from paid posts. TikTok rewards personality and original ideas, not copied trends, so it costs more thought per post. Only 56% of brands can track bookings from paid ads, so measure covers, not likes.

Start from your guest, not the app. A neighbourhood bistro whose regulars are 35 to 50 lives on Instagram. A late, loud, younger concept may need TikTok as well. Score each platform on four things: does my guest use it, can we post at the median rate, does our food or room suit its format, and does it lead to a booking. Pick the top one, add a second only if you can sustain it.

lessons.atWork: Ask ten guests tonight how they first heard of you. Tally the answers by source and age band. If social is rare, put the effort into giving people a reason to recommend you. If one platform keeps coming up, that is your first channel.
lessons.takeaway: Be excellent on one platform your guests actually use. A dead second account does more harm than having none.

news.headline: Restaurant tips have halved since 2022 as bills climb
news.gist: SumUp data shows the average UK restaurant tip fell 51%, from £5.78 in 2022 to £2.84, while average bills rose 63%.

read.what: Payments firm SumUp found the average UK restaurant tip dropped 51% since 2022, from £5.78 to £2.84, while average transaction values rose 63%. The share of restaurant payments that included a tip rose from 2.1% to 10.8%. Across all UK businesses, tips fell 20% since 2022, 13% in the past year. Leeds has the highest average tip at £5.22, Liverpool the lowest at £1.73.
read.how: More guests now tip, but each gives less: tipping has spread from a few big tippers to many small card tips. The report notes the government withdrew its updated tipping code of practice earlier in 2026, which would have made businesses consult staff on tip policies.
read.soWhat: If your team's take-home relies on tips, it may be falling even in a busy month. That matters for keeping good people, and for how you plan pay at your own place.
read.take: Compare your tip total per cover this month with the same month last year. If it has fallen, tell the team the numbers and review how tips are prompted at the card machine.

news.headline: London lunches up almost 50%, and more people eat alone
news.gist: The first EatClub Restaurant Index finds London weekday lunch visits up nearly 50% on last year and solo diners' share of tables up almost a fifth.

read.what: Dining deals app EatClub's first Restaurant Index covers six UK cities. In London, weekday lunchtime dining rose nearly 50% year on year, while evenings did not rise the same way, and solo diners' share of tables grew by almost a fifth. Diners in Liverpool are 62% more likely than Londoners to eat in groups of four or more. Average booking lead time is 38 minutes in London. Since summer, London steakhouse visits rose 41%.
read.how: These are bookings made through one app, so they show how its users behave, not the whole market. Short lead times point to late, spur-of-the-moment decisions.
read.soWhat: Lunch and solo guests are growing in London. A good counter or bar seat and a fast lunch offer can fill hours that used to be quiet.
read.take: Look at how you seat a solo guest at lunch. Give them a good seat, not the one by the kitchen door, and a menu that fits a 45-minute break.

news.headline: Ikoyi is the only UK restaurant in the World's 50 Best
news.gist: Asador Etxebarri in Spain is No. 1. Jeremy Chan's Ikoyi on the Strand fell from 15th to 48th and is the only UK entry in the top 50.

read.what: The World's 50 Best Restaurants 2026 was announced in Lima. Asador Etxebarri, near Bilbao, is No. 1, followed by Gaggan in Bangkok, Alchemist in Copenhagen, Quintonil in Mexico City and Wing in Hong Kong. Ikoyi, Jeremy Chan's restaurant at 180 The Strand, is the only UK restaurant in the top 50, at 48, down from 15 last year. London's Kol is 70th and The Ledbury 83rd.
read.soWhat: London's place at the very top has slipped. Lists like this move bookings from abroad, so watch which cities and styles rise: this year Spain and Asia lead.
read.take: Ask your team which restaurants on the list they would most like to eat at, and why. It is a cheap way to talk about what makes great hospitality.

news.headline: Three-star Moor Hall gives hospitality staff 20% off on Sundays
news.gist: Mark Birchall's Moor Hall in Lancashire now offers anyone working in hospitality 20% off Sunday bookings, with no end date.

read.what: Moor Hall, Mark Birchall's three-Michelin-star restaurant in Aughton, Lancashire, is offering 20% off every Sunday to anyone who works in hospitality. Guests add 'Industry discount' to the booking notes and the team gets in touch. The lunch menu is £155 a person and the Provenance menu £285. Wine pairings run from £165 to £325, with a soft pairing at £85. The offer runs indefinitely.
read.soWhat: Industry nights fill quiet services with guests who spread the word, and they help a team learn from peers. A 20% cut on a slow day can pay back in staff, reviews and recommendations.
read.take: Book a team visit to a top kitchen that offers a trade rate, and set one thing to watch: the welcome, the pace or the goodbye.

news.headline: Wright Brothers opens in Covent Garden on 28 November
news.gist: The seafood group takes the old Margot site at 45 Great Queen Street, with fruits de mer platters and an oyster gelato. Opening is set for 28 November.

read.what: Wright Brothers will open at 45 Great Queen Street, WC2, in the former Margot site, on 28 November. Kevin Gratton, who worked with Mark Hix, writes the menus, and Jaspal Flora, previously at 45 Jermyn Street, is head chef. Dishes include butter-grilled oysters with black winter truffle, ink-braised cuttlefish with sea aster, stacked fruits de mer platters and oyster gelato with olive oil and caviar.
read.soWhat: This is a preview: the restaurant is not open yet. A big seafood room needs a strong shellfish routine on the floor: clear allergen checks and a slick platter service.
read.take: If shellfish is on your menu, test your team on the allergen script for one platter this week.

news.headline: Paris lobster roll spot Homer Lobster lands in Soho on 1 December
news.gist: Homer Lobster opens its first permanent London site at 5 D'Arblay Street, Soho, on 1 December, led by a lobster and crayfish roll.

read.what: Paris favourite Homer Lobster opens on 1 December at 5 D'Arblay Street, W1, the former Happiness matcha bar. The signature is a lobster and crayfish roll. Other sandwiches include a crab roll, a tuna melt, salmon pastrami and a lobster grilled cheese, and any of them can be topped with caviar. Homer ran a two-week pop-up on the Southbank just over a year ago.
read.soWhat: This is a preview. It shows a growing model: a tight menu built on one luxury ingredient, in a small site, tested first as a pop-up.
read.take: Before you sign a lease, ask whether a short pop-up could test your idea first, as this brand did.

try.title: Give two wines a one-line site story
steps: Pick two wines by the glass from different places, one cool and one warm.
For each, look up latitude, height and soil, and note which way the best slopes face.
Write one line each on what the site does to the taste, such as 'high and cool, so it stays fresh'.
Share both lines at pre-shift and ask each server to use one at a table tonight.
try.why: Guests remember a place more than a grape. A short, true line about the site turns a price into a reason, and it builds your team's confidence with wine one bottle at a time.

quiz.q: Two vineyards sit on the same hillside. Which spot is most at risk of spring frost?
options: The top of the slope, highest up
The middle of the slope, facing the sun
The valley floor at the bottom
Any spot near stony, slate soil
quiz.why: Cold air is heavy and drains downhill, pooling on the valley floor in a frost pocket. Mid-slope sites stay warmer on calm, clear nights.

quiz.q: A guest asks why a Mendoza Malbec grown above 1,000 m tastes fresh despite strong sun. What is the best answer?
options: Height: air cools about 0.6°C per 100 m
The vines are planted in heavy clay
Mendoza is closer to the equator
The river reflects light onto the vines
quiz.why: WSET says air cools by about 0.6°C for every 100 m of height. Above 1,000 m that slows ripening and keeps freshness.

quiz.q: You apply for a new premises licence and nobody makes a representation. What must the council do?
options: Hold a hearing anyway, to be safe
Grant it, with conditions that fit your schedule
Send it to the police to approve
Pass it to a sub-committee of three
quiz.why: Section 18 and para 1.16 of the guidance say that with no relevant representations the authority must grant, with conditions consistent with the operating schedule.

quiz.q: A neighbour objects only because they dislike the owner's other bar. What can the council do?
options: It must hold a full hearing on the objection
It must refuse the licence until the neighbour agrees
Reject it as frivolous or vexatious, with reasons
It must refer the objection to the Home Office
quiz.why: A representation must be about the licensing objectives. The council can reject an other person's objection as frivolous or vexatious, but must give reasons.

quiz.q: Your guests are mostly 35 to 50 and you can post about 4 times a week. Where should you start?
options: TikTok, as engagement is highest
Instagram, where that age group follows
Every platform at once, to be seen
Facebook, as paid posts are cheap
quiz.why: Instagram's biggest hospitality follower group is 35 to 44, it is the most influential platform for social-led guests (44%), and 4 posts a week is its median.

terms.def: The direction a vineyard slope faces. A slope facing the equator gets more sun and warmth.
A low spot, such as a valley floor, where heavy cold air pools on still nights and frost hits vines hardest.
A panel of three councillors from the council's licensing committee that holds hearings and decides contested licence applications.
An objection or comment that is about the four licensing objectives, made in time by a responsible authority or other person, and not frivolous or vexatious.
Anyone who is not a responsible authority, such as a resident or nearby business, who makes a representation about a licence.
The share of people who react to a post, such as liking, commenting or sharing, out of those who see it or follow the account.

toolkit.name: Five site questions for any wine
items: Latitude: is it in the 30 to 50 degree band, and nearer which end?
Height: how high are the vines? Each 100 m is about 0.6°C cooler.
Slope: which way does it face, and is it mid-slope or on the valley floor?
Water: is there a river, lake or ocean near to cool, warm or reflect light?
Soil: does it drain freely and hold heat, like slate, or hold water, like clay?

toolkit.name: Who can object: licence contact list
items: Council licensing officer and the committee clerk
Fire and rescue, planning, and health and safety
Child protection body and public health
In London, the Greater London Authority
Nearest residents' group and neighbouring businesses

toolkit.name: One-platform test
items: Guests: do most of mine use it? Ask ten guests how they found us.
Effort: can we post at the median rate (Instagram 4 a week, TikTok 2)?
Format: do our food and room suit photos, short video or both?
Booking pull: can a follower book in two taps from the profile?
Choose the top scorer. Add a second only when the first is steady.
